To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CBI reforms matter in countries with high inflation, but not in low-inflation ones.
CBI reforms have contributed to reducing the inflation rate in countries with high inflation, but not in countries with low inflation.
CBI reforms have contributed to bringing high inflation down to low inflation in the long-run, but have not affected inflation performance in countries where inflation is already low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the reforms of the central bank independence that have taken place in many countries during the last two decades have had any impact on inflation performance.
the question whether CBI reforms have mattered for inflation performance in countries with a high inflation rate.
whether central bank independence reforms matter for the inflation performance of countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CBI reforms have been effective, but only for countries with high inflation.
the effects are positive but small, and that the effects are stronger when CBI-reforms occur in countries with high inflation rates, but not in countries with low inflation rates.
CBI-reforms matter for inflation performance, but only for countries with a high inflation rate before the reform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CBI-reforms have contributed to the reduction of the number of inflation episodes and the duration of those episodes.
CBI-reforms matter in countries where they are needed most, but that they are not a panacea for inflation problems.
CBI reforms have been a necessary but not a sufficient condition for bringing inflation down.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CBI literature has been too focused on the effects of CBI in the presence of high inflation, whereas CBI reforms may be more relevant for countries that have not experienced high inflation.
the impact of CBI reforms on inflation performance is heterogeneous, depending on the initial inflation level, the degree of central bank independence and the type of reform.
CBI reforms do not appear to matter for inflation performance in countries with low inflation.
